newsitem.title: USA: Banc One to buy Liberty Bancorp.
newsitem.headline: Banc One to buy Liberty Bancorp.

text.p: Banc One Corp., one of the nation's largest banks, agreed to acquire Liberty Bancorp Inc., another Midwestern bank holding company, for $546 million in stock, the companies said Monday.
Industry analysts said the deal fit Banc One's strategy of being one of the biggest banks in markets where it operates.
The acquisition will make Banc One the largest banking company in Oklahoma City, Okla., where Liberty is based, and one of the top banking companies in the state, the companies said.
Columbus, Ohio-based Banc One operates 59 banks in 12 states stretching from West Virginia to Arizona and is the 10th largest bank holding company in the nation.
Liberty operates 29 banking offices in Oklahoma City and Tulsa, Okla.
"This is an important affiliation for us in that our stated objective is to be one of the top three banks in the markets we serve," Banc One Chairman John McCoy said in a statement.
Under the agreement, Liberty shareholders will receive 1.175 shares of Banc One for each share of Liberty.
Liberty stock jumped $8.75 to $50.50 on Nasdaq and Banc One fell 12.5 cents to $44.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
"It's an opportunistic deal for (Banc One)," said Nancy Bush, an analyst with Brown Brothers Harriman.
"They had a very, very small presence in Oklahoma -- (about) $600 million in assets, which made them an also-ran in the state -- and they take it up to No. 2" in Oklahoma with the Liberty deal.
Overall, Banc One had assets of $98.6 billion and Liberty had assets of about $2.9 billion as of Sept 30.

"They're buying a very good franchise in Liberty," Joseph Stieven, an analyst with Stifel Nicolaus, said. "They don't have to pay a lot of money to get very significant market share... (and) Oklahoma is a great market."
Joseph Duwan, an analyst with Keefe Bruyette & Woods, said Banc One expected to prune Liberty's expenses and saw revenue opportunities, particularly in loan generation.
Brown Brothers' Bush said she expected more acquisitions from Banc One.
"(Liberty) is not the big deal everybody's been looking for," she said. "I don't think this will be enough to alleviate the speculation that there is another larger deal coming up in '97."
The merger is subject to approval by state and federal regulators and by Liberty shareholders. The companies said they expect the deal to close by mid-1997.
